summary: Complete expert bundles, phase-aware admission, bank planning and temporary cache memory loans
implementation_scope: Python cache/bundle ownership, phase-aware host admission, physical bank/copy planning and C++ slot/region-loan state machines; actual backend transfers and projection are external

agent_guidance.use_when: Routed weight reuse can repay cache management when preferred-device capacity is limited
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Reuse is poor, weights already fit, or exact direct access/static placement is cheaper
provides: Byte-bounded ready-object cache with leases and settled-only eviction
Fixed-slot complete-component upload/publication and protected uses
C++ slot generations, upload/use identities and sequence exhaustion guards
Temporary contiguous cache-region loans, transactional survivor relocation, private operation owners, settled return and graph-binding invalidation
Slot loans over any set of slots so an owner that lent memory to the cache (unreachable KV positions, an idle workspace) reclaims it with the same lifecycle and gets it back empty
Phase-aware population/read-only reuse with protected reads that preserve replacement ages
Compatible-layout bank budgets including guards/alignment and dual-contiguous component copy runs
Original-demand occurrence/unique counts with caller-measured phase/mode transfer and synchronization costs
engine_supplies: Representation-complete keys/component layouts, initialized guards and actual bank/map/staging reservations
Actual copies, ordered READY publication and operation-specific receipts
Loan region/survivor policy, complete contiguous slot geometry, scratch alignment and lifetime retention through failed-drain recovery
Projection, policy selection, teardown and backend failure recovery

All components ready before publication; all readers settled before overwrite
Failed overwrite never resurrects old content; account actual physical bytes
Loans alias one charged backing reservation; all copy and scratch dependencies settle before capacity returns
adapt: Replacement/admission policy and pool capacity, including decayed original-demand scores and measured marginal benefit per byte
Key, component layout and metadata representation
Host or device management and integration with a fused backend
Population token bound, layout-group budget shares and native transfer granularity

code_files.purpose: Python byte-cache leases and complete-component bundle directory with retained upload/use identities
C++ content directory with protected acquisitions, settled publication, transactional region loans/relocation, retained operation owners and binding generations
Runnable native host copy/scratch/refill example with one retained Core backing reservation
Phase-aware exact cache admission, compatible bank sizing, coalesced component ranges and cost observations
Runnable host byte-storage POC for complete staging, exact fallback and read-only prefill

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ for reference protocols; C++20 for the slot directory; device integration requires its chosen backend
requires.model: Expert-routed computation with caller-defined revisions, layouts, encodings and complete bundles
requires.workload: Repeated routed demands under a bounded memory envelope; profitability depends on locality and miss costs

contract.input: Representation-complete expert keys and exact extents; fixed slot-indexed component encodings/extents, reserved backing owners and ticket-bound enqueue receipts; explicit workload phase, complete bank geometry/budget and unique expert/slot copy pairs
contract.output: Owner leases or ready slot/generation maps and unique bundle upload/use identities; admission, physically sized bank spans, component transfer ranges and phase/mode observations; generation-bound loan/copy/borrow handles and exclusive scratch extents
contract.ownership: Directory owns serialized metadata and retains caller-reserved backing/staging owners. Every read remains protected until settlement; complete upload publication waits for all component copies. Register loan copies/borrowers before enqueue and retain the directory until close succeeds. Ambiguous submissions require physical quiescence before settlement; loans keep their backing reservation charged once.
contract.failure: Reject protected/loading exhaustion, duplicate or foreign tickets/uses, missing components, stale receipts, encoding/extent mismatch and unsettled publication. Failed copies leave overwritten content empty. C++ sequence exhaustion cannot wrap identities.
contract.core_boundary: Consumer owns expert representation/reuse policy. Core supplies byte reservations, allocation and CUDA readiness.

dependencies: crit Core resources for loan_example.cpp only

validation.host: Python fixtures cover bundle publication, phase/bank/copy planning and failures. Native CPU fixtures cover loan admission, overlap/fragmentation, protected regions, partial relocation failure, independent sessions, retained owners, binding invalidation and 1,250 real byte-copy loan/return cycles, and reverse slot loans (scattered slots, a live reader blocking a reclaim, survivor relocation, empty return, 500 repeated requests); the example checks Core reservation lifetime.
validation.native: Native cache transfers, device publication, encoded projections and model behavior remain unqualified by host fixtures
validation.performance: Unmeasured for a native engine; host fixture success is not a speed claim
